notes: The supplied description and page do not specify the model term, emotion/error category, or comparison needed to identify a unique target. No target was assigned from audit ID, input order, or numeric matching. All statistics below are candidates only; none is a row-specific extraction. Section 3.2 uses a TASK × EMOTION × GROUP RT ANOVA across all three tasks, rather than a uniquely identified emotion-task-only contrast. Candidates: TASK F1.7,146.1 = 947.0, p < .001, partial eta squared .917; EMOTION F3.6,311.2 = 93.0, p < .001, partial eta squared .519; TASK × EMOTION F4.7,405.1 = 99.5, p < .001, partial eta squared .536; GROUP main effect/interactions collectively Fs ≤ 1.4, ps > .05. The four identical RT descriptions do not identify four individual terms. Candidate participant counts: the explicitly separate final HC, AN, and MD groups contain 37, 26, and 26 girls. For a three-group critical ANOVA, 37 + 26 + 26 = 89 participants; for AN versus MD, 26 + 26 = 52; for HC versus AN or HC versus MD, 37 + 26 = 63. These are conditional candidate analytic sums, not selected row N values. Medication sensitivity exclusions were nine AN and seven MD participants, but the paper reports findings based on the whole sample. No N was inferred from degrees of freedom. Original fields only were assigned. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. PDF pages 4–6 rendered and visually inspected; canonical text is the evidence source. No effect-size conversions performed.
